title: Water First
can_do: 说出身体需要，并说明先要什么，让成人及时提供帮助。
trigger: After quiet play, Mom suggests a break and he notices that he is thirsty.
stretch_response: Can I have water first, please?
repair_response: Water first, please, not a snack.
setting: A quiet break at the home table after play.
essential_props: one tray with a blue cup of water and a small snack

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: I have water and a snack.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Can I have water first, please?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: That's better. I'm not thirsty now.

replay_cards.title: A snack after drawing
replay_cards.change: He feels hungry while Mom has a drink and a small snack available
replay_cards.challenge: Say the hunger need and ask for the snack first. Mom hands it over promptly; he eats a little, then says whether he wants the drink. No food is withheld for a sentence.

replay_cards.title: Water before the car ride
replay_cards.setting: Beside the parked car before a short trip
replay_cards.change: He feels thirsty and Dad also has a snack ready
replay_cards.challenge: Tell Dad the need. If Dad initially offers the snack, clarify 'Water first, please, not a snack.' Dad promptly provides the bottle; he drinks while stationary, then gets ready to buckle in.

parent_support: Acknowledge thirst immediately and make water available; do not require a complete sentence, please, or a second choice before he can drink.
Offer only the water and snack that are already available. Accept water first and let him decide whether he wants the snack afterward.
Let him take a comfortable sip before he reports how he feels; do not make him speak with water in his mouth.
